summary: A hands-on tutorial slide deck from Open Robotics (Mabel M. Zhang) for the ICRA 2023 workshop MT28 'All about ROS 2 and the new Gazebo', held 29 May 2023. It walks attendees through setting up a Docker environment with Gazebo Garden, then covers the gz command line interface, the gz sim GUI with example worlds, dynamic level-of-detail loading, a lidar sensor tutorial, writing a Gazebo system plugin via the Entity Component System concept, and a Turtlebot 4 ROS interoperability case study, ending with community involvement resources.
one_line: Hands-on ICRA 2023 tutorial slides teaching Gazebo Garden's CLI, GUI, sensors, plugins and ROS 2 integration.
key_facts: The tutorial was ICRA 2023 tutorial MT28 'All about ROS 2 and the new Gazebo', held 29 May 2023, and was presented by Mabel M. Zhang, Ph.D. of the Open Robotics team at Intrinsic.
The recommended setup is an Ubuntu Jammy (22.04) system with some kind of GPU, with Gazebo Garden installed in advance or via the Docker image of about 2 GB.
The demo Docker image is started with ./run.bash osrf/icra2023_ros2_gz_tutorial:tutorial_nvidia from the cloned icra2023_ros2_gz_tutorial/docker directory.
The tutorial slides recommend that conference attendees avoid downloading the 2 GB Docker image over conference WiFi and instead pass a USB stick between pairs.
The gz topic command with -l lists topics, -e -t echoes a topic, and -i -t gives topic info.
Gazebo's default physics engine is DART (gz-physics-dartsim-plugin) and its default render engine is OGRE2 (ogre2).
The gz sim option -v takes a verbosity level from 0 to 4, and -r runs the simulation on start.
Dynamic level-of-detail loading is described as a concept for large worlds that load models based on distance from the robot, and it was used in DARPA SubT.
In the levels.sdf tutorial, the blue vehicle is commanded with linear x of 4.0 and the red vehicle with linear x of 2.0 through gz topic cmd_vel messages.
The sensors tutorial's lidar_node.cc subscribes to /lidar and publishes gz.msgs.Twist messages to /cmd_vel with linear x set to 0.5, so the robot turns as it detects a wall.
The CMakeLists.txt for the lidar example finds gz-transport12 and links the lidar_node executable against gz-transport12::core.

Gazebo system plugins implement interfaces including ISystemConfigure (once, at load), ISystemPreUpdate (before each physics step), ISystemUpdate, ISystemPostUpdate (after each physics step, ECM read-only), and ISystemReset.
The thermal camera example sets a model temperature of 285.0 via the gz::sim::systems::Thermal plugin and a thermal sensor with min_temp 253.15, max_temp 673.15 and resolution 3.0.
The Turtlebot 4 case study uses the third-party turtlebot4_simulator package, which is based on ROS 2 Humble and Gazebo Fortress rather than Garden.
